best_architecture: For Local-Claw, use an event-stream-driven ReAct loop with an optional upfront Plan-Execute-Monitor pass and Reflexion-style error recovery, running on an explicit state graph with durable checkpointing. Backbone: the OpenHands/CodeAct design where the agent is a step(state) -> action function over a chronological event stream of (action, observation) pairs, and actions are executable code/tool calls (bash, python via a persistent IPython kernel, file edits) rather than ad-hoc JSON schemas. CodeAct (executable-code actions) outperforms text/JSON action formats because the LLM emits code it was heavily pretrained on and a single action can compose control flow - especially valuable for a smaller local brain (Gemma 4 MoE / Qwen2.5-Coder-32B). Layer three loop refinements: (1) ReAct (Thought->Action->Observation) as the per-step inner loop; (2) a lightweight upfront Plan-Execute-Monitor wrapper that decomposes the task before execution - empirically the ReAct+Plan hybrid beats both vanilla ReAct (83%->95%) and full Tree-of-Thoughts (~100x compute and it did NOT surpass ReAct+Plan), so AVOID ToT as the default loop and reserve branching search for isolated hard subproblems only; (3) Reflexion as the error-recovery layer - on test/build failure an evaluator scores the result and a self-reflection module writes a natural-language diagnosis into an episodic memory buffer that conditions the next attempt, under a max-iterations cap. Design decisions that matter most, in priority order: (a) Agent-Computer Interface (ACI) quality - SWE-Agent's central finding is that purpose-built, concise tools (scoped file viewer with line numbers, syntax-checking edit command, search_file/search_dir) dominate raw shell access; invest here first. (b) Sandboxed execution - run all actions in a Docker container with a persistent bash + IPython kernel so state carries across steps. (c) State as the core abstraction - model the loop as an explicit graph (LangGraph) with per-thread checkpointing to MongoDB so a long coding task can pause for human approval, survive crashes/timeouts, and resume or time-travel/replay. (d) Repo-map context management - a Tree-sitter ranked-symbol graph (Aider's approach) so the agent requests only relevant files instead of stuffing the whole repo into a limited local context window. (e) Architect/editor model split - keep reasoning and editing as separate calls/configs: Gemma 4 as architect, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B as editor. (f) Bounded loops with explicit termination - cap turns, detect unproductive loops (ReAct myopia), git-commit each successful edit so every step is a recoverable checkpoint. Map onto the asyncio orchestrator: the ReAct/Plan-Execute-Monitor loop is the inner step function, MCP stdio tools are the action space wrapped as a SWE-Agent-style ACI, MongoDB/Chroma/Redis back the Reflexion episodic + long-term memory, and a LangGraph checkpointer (or custom asyncio checkpoint to Mongo/Redis) provides resume/replay.

pitfalls: ReAct 'myopia' / stuck loops: the agent repeats the same action or observation without progress, trapped in a local reasoning loop. Fix: explicit stuck-detection - track the last N actions; if N consecutive actions are identical (or no environment state change), escalate from the inner ReAct loop to a fresh Plan-Execute pass or a Reflexion step rather than continuing to burn turns.

Context window saturation on long coding tasks: the event stream grows to fill the full window and squeezes out the current code context, degrading reasoning (context pollution / context rot). Fix: actively compress/summarize early history with a reversible compaction policy - drop re-derivable content (full file bodies, stale tool outputs) and re-read on demand, keep a structured note of decisions and TODOs; do NOT let the raw EventLog grow unbounded into the prompt.

Unsafe tool ACI: a raw bash shell without sandboxing risks rm -rf / and other host damage when the agent improvises. Fix: execute every action inside a Docker container with no host mount for the agent's writable workspace; the host filesystem must be unaffected by anything the agent runs.

Monolithic tool schema: a single giant execute_code tool that accepts arbitrary Python is impossible for the LLM to use correctly and invites parameter hallucination. Fix (SWE-Agent finding): scoped, concise tools with clear argument names (view, edit-with-syntax-check, search_file, run_tests) dramatically outperform; expose specialist tooling behind delegated sub-agents, not a flat 100-tool list.

No git checkpoint between steps: if step 8 fails catastrophically with no commits since step 1, the working state is unrecoverable. Fix: git-commit after every successful file edit so the git log is a rollback ladder allowing partial recovery to any prior good step.

Reflexion without episodic memory persistence: self-reflection that is not stored across attempts repeats the same mistake. Fix: write each reflection to an episodic memory buffer (Redis hot, Mongo durable) and condition the next attempt on the retrieved reflections.

Tree-of-Thoughts as the default top-level loop: ~100x the compute of ReAct+Plan and empirically does NOT beat it at equal budget, and each node runs real tools against the repo. Fix: use ToT/LATS only for bounded isolated sub-decisions (candidate localization, patch selection/voting), never as the driver.

Architect and editor in the same model call: architect reasoning and edit-output generation interfere, producing sloppy diffs. Fix: keep them as separate litellm calls or separate model configs (Gemma 4 architect call -> Qwen2.5-Coder-32B editor call).

Goal drift over long horizons: after many turns and summarizations the agent drifts to unrelated tasks. Fix: an editable persistent plan as a stable anchor, a well-crafted system prompt, and a Monitor step that reverts (git checkout) and re-runs from a refined plan on mismatch instead of patching forward.

No explicit termination/budget control: open-ended loops thrash and burn tokens. Fix: a controller enforcing max iterations, token/cost budget, and timeouts, with AgentFinishAction as the only clean exit and best-so-far state persisted on a budget halt.

Overfitting the scaffold to SWE-bench Verified: live-benchmark resolve rates are dramatically lower (e.g., >60% Verified vs much lower on SWE-bench-Live/Pro). Fix: validate the ACI/prompts on live or held-out tasks, not a static set.

  Scenario: Resolve a failing test via the ReAct+Plan loop within budget
    Given a sandboxed workspace cloned at a target repository commit
    And a failing test that defines the task
    And an editable plan generated by the Plan-Execute-Monitor pass
    When the orchestrator runs the inner ReAct/CodeAct loop
    And each code action is executed in the Docker runtime and returns an observation
    Then the failing test passes in 10 iterations or fewer
    And the agent emits an AgentFinishAction with a unified-diff patch
    And the EventLog contains the full ordered action/observation trajectory

  Scenario: Reflexion error recovery avoids repeating a known mistake
    Given the agent has made the same failing edit twice
    When the controller routes the second failure into a Reflexion step
    And the reflection is written to episodic memory
    And the third attempt queries that episodic memory
    Then the third attempt explicitly avoids the previously reflected failure mode
    And the agent does not re-issue the identical failed edit

  Scenario: Docker sandbox isolates a destructive command from the host
    Given the agent issues an action equivalent to rm -rf /
    When the action is executed inside the Docker sandbox container
    Then only the container filesystem is affected
    And the host filesystem is unaffected
    And the orchestrator records the destructive action as an observation and continues safely

  Scenario: Git checkpoint per edit enables partial rollback
    Given the agent performs 5 successful file edits in sequence
    When each successful edit completes
    Then git log shows 5 new commits, one per edit
    And the orchestrator can roll back to any of the prior 5 commits on a later catastrophic failure

  Scenario: Stuck-detection escalates out of a ReAct loop
    Given the agent emits N consecutive identical actions with no state change
    When the stuck-detector trips
    Then the inner ReAct loop is escalated to a fresh Plan-Execute pass
    And the orchestrator does not continue emitting the repeated action
optimal_implementation:
Implement a CodingOrchestrator class over four decoupled primitives (Agent, Workspace/Runtime, LLM via litellm, Controller) plus an outer Plan-Execute-Monitor loop, with an explicit event-stream accumulator, stuck-detection, a Docker sandbox wrapper, and the Gemma->Qwen architect/editor routing.

Core types (pydantic v2):
  class Action(BaseModel): kind: str; payload: dict        # subclasses: RunCmd, RunPython, EditFile, FinishTask
  class Observation(BaseModel): stdout: str; stderr: str; exit_code: int; ok: bool
  class Subtask(BaseModel): id: int; goal: str; done: bool = False

Event-stream accumulator (the chronological trajectory):
  self.events: list[dict] = []   # each: {"action": Action, "observation": Observation}

Main class:
  class CodingOrchestrator:
      def __init__(self, llm, workspace, memory, max_iter=10, stuck_n=3):
          self.events=[]; self.recent_actions=[]; ...

      async def run_task(self, task_description: str) -> Result:
          plan = await self._plan(task_description)            # list[Subtask] via Gemma architect
          for subtask in plan:
              for i in range(self.max_iter):
                  action = await self._execute(subtask)        # next action via MCP tool / Qwen editor
                  if self._is_stuck(action):                   # stuck-detection
                      plan = await self._plan(task_description) # escalate: re-plan
                      break
                  obs = await self.workspace.execute(action)   # Docker sandbox
                  self.events.append({"action": action, "observation": obs})
                  status = self._monitor(obs)                  # test/linter check
                  if status == "pass":
                      self._git_checkpoint(f"subtask {subtask.id}: {subtask.goal}")
                      subtask.done = True; break
                  if status == "fail":
                      await self._reflect(obs)                  # episodic memory write
          return self._finalize()

  Plan-Execute-Monitor + Reflexion helpers:
      async def _plan(self, task) -> list[Subtask]:            # one architect call; editable markdown plan
          return parse_plan(await self._architect(task))
      async def _execute(self, subtask) -> Action:             # ReAct step conditioned on events + memory
          ctx = self._build_state(subtask, self.events, self.memory.recall())
          return parse_action(await self._editor(ctx))
      def _monitor(self, obs) -> str:                          # 'pass' | 'fail' | 'continue'
          return classify_test_output(obs)
      async def _reflect(self, obs):
          reflection = await self._architect(reflect_prompt(self.events, obs))
          self.memory.add(reflection)                          # Redis hot + Mongo durable
      def _is_stuck(self, action) -> bool:
          self.recent_actions.append(action.kind + str(action.payload))
          self.recent_actions = self.recent_actions[-self.stuck_n:]
          return len(self.recent_actions)==self.stuck_n and len(set(self.recent_actions))==1
      def _git_checkpoint(self, message):
          subprocess.run(["git","-C",self.repo,"add","-A"]); subprocess.run(["git","-C",self.repo,"commit","-m",message])

  Docker sandbox wrapper (host filesystem never mounted writable):
      def execute(self, action) -> Observation:
          proc = subprocess.run(["docker","exec",self.container,"bash","-lc", action.payload["cmd"]],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=self.timeout)
          return Observation(stdout=proc.stdout, stderr=proc.stderr, exit_code=proc.returncode, ok=proc.returncode==0)

  litellm architect/editor routing (separate calls / configs):
      async def _architect(self, prompt):    # planning + reflection: Gemma 4
          r = await litellm.acompletion(model="openai/gemma-4-moe", api_base=GEMMA_URL, messages=[{"role":"user","content":prompt}])
          return r.choices[0].message.content
      async def _editor(self, prompt):        # code/edit generation: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B
          r = await litellm.acompletion(model="openai/qwen2.5-coder-32b", api_base=QWEN_URL, messages=[{"role":"user","content":prompt}])
          return r.choices[0].message.content

Put in the spec: the four-primitive separation; CodeAct (executable code) action space; the scoped ACI tool set (view/edit-with-syntax-check/search/run_tests) wrapped over MCP stdio; the event-stream accumulator; stuck-detection (N identical actions -> re-plan); Docker sandbox with no writable host mount; git-checkpoint after every successful edit; Reflexion-on-failure with persistent episodic memory; reversible context compaction; the Gemma-architect / Qwen-editor litellm split; and the controller budget/termination contract (max_iter, token budget, AgentFinishAction as the only clean exit).
sota_improvements: SWE-bench Lite/Verified leaders use distinct orchestration patterns worth borrowing selectively: Augment + Claude Opus 4.6 tops the 2026 leaderboard (~72% Verified) on a tuned agentic scaffold; Moatless Tools (search/edit-tool agent), Agentless (non-agentic), and CodeR show the scaffold matters as much as the backbone - benchmark Local-Claw's ACI against these rather than chasing a bigger local model.

Add Agentless (arxiv:2407.01489) as a cheap non-agentic fast path: hierarchical localization -> diff-format patch generation -> patch validation, no LLM-decided control flow. It hit 27.33% on SWE-bench Lite at $0.34/issue - competitive with full ReAct at a fraction of the compute, ideal as Local-Claw's first-attempt tier before escalating to the agentic loop.

Adopt OpenHands micro-agent specialization: split the monolithic agent into specialized micro-agents (Coder/Editor, Verifier/test-runner, Resolver/localizer) coordinated by the controller; specialized micro-agents outperform a single generalist agent and keep each agent's context small.

Reserve LATS (Language Agent Tree Search, arxiv:2310.04406) - MCTS over the action space with LM value functions + self-reflection - for isolated hard subproblems only; it is markedly better than random beam search on hard problems (92.7% pass@1 HumanEval with GPT-4) but costs 10-30x, so gate it behind difficulty/stuck-detection rather than running it as the default loop.

Use Claude Code's production architecture as the SOTA reference for the agentic tier: computer-use-style tool execution plus multi-agent spawning (a lead agent that forks fresh sub-agents with minimal scoped context for discrete subtasks), which combats KV-cache bloat and context confusion - mirror this with selective-sharing sub-agent delegation in the asyncio orchestrator.

Make context compaction a first-class reversible policy (strip re-derivable info, re-read on demand) instead of naive truncation/summarization, and add persistent cross-session note-taking so the orchestrator warms up on a given codebase across runs.

Treat the ACI as a tuned, evaluated component (SWE-agent grid-search methodology): A/B the command set and feedback messages on a dev split, and validate against live/held-out benchmarks (SWE-bench-Live, SWE-bench-Pro) to avoid overfitting the scaffold to Verified.
